title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Longue Marche, c. 1981; Galois-group version of the birational anabelian programme). K is a field finitely generated over Q. Σ_K (written E_K on the previous page) = Gal(K̄/K) is viewed as an extension 1→Π_K→Σ_K→Γ_Q, where Π_K = Gal(K̄/K·Q̄) is the 'geometric' part and the image of Σ_K in Γ_Q is open. On the previous page Grothendieck asked whether, for an outer homomorphism Σ_{K'}→Σ_K over Γ_Q, the following are equivalent: (a) it comes from an embedding K⊂K'; (b) it has open image; (c) it is 'admissible'. He added in the margin that (c) is not strong enough. He drew a consequence of the conjecture: sections of Σ_K→Γ_Q over an open Γ' would have nontrivial centralizer in Σ_K. Since their centralizer in Γ is trivial, one would get Π_K^{Γ'} ≠ 1.

This page corrects that. 'Ceci est sans doute faux.' The reason is a weight/twist phenomenon. A section coming from a rational point of a model has an inertia part isomorphic to Ẑ(1)^d. Γ' acts on it through the cyclotomic character, so it has no Γ'-fixed points, but it is fixed by Γ'^o = ker(χ_cycl|Γ').

He therefore strengthens (c) to (c'): the homomorphism Σ^o_{K'}→Σ_K, i.e. the restriction to the kernel of Σ_{K'}→Γ_Q→Ẑ* (cyclotomic character), should satisfy the condition. This is plausibly 'est admissible'; the words are illegible.

To see that (c') is necessary for 'geometric' homomorphisms, he needs a lemma. For every open Σ'⊂Σ_K, the centralizer in Σ_K not only of Σ' but even of Σ'^o is trivial. This would follow from the proof of 'Th. 1' (centralizer-freeness) together with a fact marked 'à vérifier!': for every open Γ'⊂Γ_Q, the centralizer of Γ'^o = Γ'∩Gal(Q̄/Q(μ_∞)) in Γ_Q is trivial.

Corrected conjectural consequence: for every section of Σ_K→Γ_Q over an open Γ' that acts effectively on Π_K (i.e. Π_K≠1), one has Π_K^{Γ'^o} ≠ 1. Equivalently, the image of Γ'^o under the section has nontrivial centralizer in Π_K. This is a necessary 'geometric' property of birational sections: each should carry a nontrivial cyclotomically-twisted inertia piece.
errors: The centralizer fact for Γ'^o is flagged by Grothendieck himself as unverified. It is plausible: Q^ab is Hilbertian, and Galois groups of Hilbertian fields have strong centralizer-freeness properties. But it is not proved on the page.
The original consequence Π_K^{Γ'}≠1 (previous page) is indeed false for point-induced sections, because of the Ẑ(1) twist. Grothendieck correctly diagnoses this.
'degré K'/Q' on the previous page must mean transcendence degree; this is implicit, not an error.
The precise property in (c') is illegible ('est [?] [?]'). The argument as written only makes sense if it is the same property as in (c), e.g. admissibility or trivial centralizer of the image.

ideas.what: An outer homomorphism of absolute Galois groups of finitely generated fields over Γ_Q comes from a field embedding iff it has open image.
ideas.modern_name: Hom-form of the birational anabelian conjecture (Mochizuki's theorem for sub-p-adic fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, letter to Faltings 1983); proved by Mochizuki 1999, with Pop for the Isom form
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (birational anabelian hints)

ideas.what: Strengthen the condition on Σ_{K'}→Σ_K by restricting to the kernel of the cyclotomic character, Σ^o_{K'}.
ideas.modern_name: Using the 'geometric-modulo-cyclotomic' subgroup / Ẑ(1)-weight considerations in anabelian reconstruction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in later work of Pop and Mochizuki (cyclotomic character reconstruction)

ideas.what: Centralizers in Γ_Q of Γ'^o = Γ'∩Gal(Q̄/Q^ab) are trivial; likewise centralizers in Σ_K of Σ'^o are trivial.
ideas.modern_name: Centralizer-freeness ('slimness') of absolute Galois groups of Hilbertian fields and their normal subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Neukirch, Ikeda, Fried–Jarden circle of results; 'slim' terminology Mochizuki

ideas.what: Every section of Σ_K→Γ_Q over open Γ' should have Π_K^{Γ'^o}≠1, i.e. a nontrivial twisted inertia part (not Π_K^{Γ'}≠1).
ideas.modern_name: Birational section conjecture / sections have nontrivial inertia Ẑ(1)^d (point-induced decomposition groups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (section conjecture, 1983); birational version studied by Koenigsmann, Pop, Esnault–Wittenberg, Stix

missed.claim: A concrete necessary condition for birational sections is proposed: the restriction of a section to the kernel of the cyclotomic character must have nontrivial fixed points in Π_K. This is derived from the Hom-conjecture plus centralizer-freeness, with the Γ'^o refinement motivated by the Ẑ(1) twist of inertia. It is a weakened, 'cyclotomic-kernel' form of the birational section conjecture. I am not aware that it is stated in this form in the literature.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Over number fields the birational section conjecture is open. A statement only about the Gal(Q̄/Q^ab)-part of sections, i.e. existence of a nonzero twisted 'inertia' element, is a weaker target. It could be approachable via Hilbertianity and slimness of G_{Q^ab}.

missed.claim: Grothendieck's own record of self-correction: admissibility of Σ_{K'}→Σ_K is insufficient, and one must test the restriction to Σ^o_{K'}. This anticipates the role of the cyclotomic character in Mochizuki's Hom-theorem proof.
missed.quote: il faudrait en renforcer c) ci-dessus en c') L'hom. Σ^o_{K'} → Σ_K
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically documents that the 'open image' Hom-criterion and the cyclotomic subtlety were already worked out c. 1981.

deep.surprise_reason: Notable unpublished detail of the pre-1983 birational anabelian programme: the Γ'^o (cyclotomic-kernel) correction to a section-centralizer consequence. However, the underlying conjectures are known and later proved or formulated, and the page is mostly a quick correction.
transcription_corrections: The group symbol is probably the same script 'ℰ' as on the previous page (ℰ_K, ℰ_{K'}), not Σ.
In c') the composite is 'ℰ_{K'} → Γ_{Q̄|Q} → Ẑ*' (from the full group, whose kernel is ℰ^o_{K'}), not 'Σ^o_{K'} → ...'.
The illegible words after 'est' in c') are probably 'admissible', consistent with condition c).
'vérifier que pour tout sous-groupe ouvert ℰ' d'un ℰ_K': '[-savoir-]' is struck.
The last lines likely read: 'Pour toute section d'un sous-groupe ouvert Γ' de Γ_Q dans ℰ_K, (opérant effectivement sur Π_K), on a (si Π_K ≠ (1)) Π_K^{Γ'^o} ≠ (1)'.
